questions.topic: Between the dates — the report-window week
questions.q: The insolvency disclosure on 28 May is:
o: A fact that EXISTED at the report date condition-wise? Evaluate whether the deterioration pre-dated 31 March: if the conditions at year-end explain it ⇒ adjust; if new ⇒ disclose — the auditor cannot simply 'ignore' before issuing
questions.why: Careful: the 'no active search' window runs AFTER the report date; here the facts arrive BEFORE issuing — the auditor evaluates whether the condition existed at the balance-sheet date (the 12 May confirmation's silence is informative); the timing decides the bucket, not the date of the phone call.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

questions.topic: Between the dates — the report-window week
o: The read of subsequent approvals; a declared dividend after year-end is a NON-adjusting event (present obligation arises with declaration ⇒ disclosure/recognise per the framework at declaration — state the cut-off logic)
questions.why: Interim facts the audit already read may not cover: the duty runs to the report date — the new item forces updated inquiry of the re-issued minutes; for dividends: declared after the reporting date ⇒ non-adjusting, disclose the amount and per-share (the recognition line: only where declaration created a present obligation by the reporting date).

questions.topic: Between the dates — the report-window week
questions.q: The correct procedure set for the period after the last fieldwork to report date:
o: Specific procedures: read minutes, latest interim FS, inquire of management/TCWG on updated positions, read the approved draft statements — exactly because the search obligation is ACTIVE until the date of the report
Only a rep letter date change
questions.why: SA 560's list — the 'designed to identify' set — that is the paragraph that turns 'nothing happened' into 'we checked whether anything did'.

questions.topic: Between the dates — the report-window week
questions.q: Management refuses to adjust the debtors for the now-insolvent account (arguing 26 May is 'next year'). The auditor:
o: Evaluate the evidence (was the deterioration at 31 March probable and estimable?); if yes, a known misstatement — qualify/adverse by pervasiveness; if genuinely post-period, insist on disclosure; escalate to TCWG in either case
questions.why: The substance test: what did the receivable look like at year-end — the 12 May unremarkable confirmation weighs against the adjust case, but the customer's cash-flow state through March is the evidence — the auditor decides the bucket and then the report consequence; refusal to DISCLOSE is also a misstatement.

questions.topic: Between the dates — the report-window week
questions.q: After the report is issued and the statements sent to the AGM, the auditor learns on 30 June of a 26 May fact that WOULD have changed the opinion:
o: The SA 560 'facts becoming known after the date of the auditor's report' route: discuss, determine if amendment needed, act so users don't rely — re-date the report or issue an additional report referring to the note
questions.why: The distinction between 'no duty to update' and 'no duty to act when an old truth surfaces': if the fact EXISTED and would have changed the report, action is required; the mechanics: management amends + auditor extends procedures to the new date (or reports on the amendment only, with the Indian framing preferring the additional-report path), and if management refuses, take steps to prevent reliance.

questions.q: After the year-end, a major customer's warehouse burns down on 14 May; the report is dated 28 May. This is:
o: Adjusting — receivable was affected by conditions after the date
Non-adjusting — the condition arose after the reporting date; disclose if material
questions.why: Type 1 (adjust) = conditions EXISTING at the reporting date (the 90-day-overdue customer's death in May confirming December's impairment); Type 2 (disclose) = conditions arising after — a new fire damages an asset whole at year-end: disclose the nature and estimate, don't restate.

mem.tip: The ledger remembers the past; the fire is tomorrow's entry.

questions.topic: No active search after report date
questions.q: Between the balance sheet date and the audit report date, the auditor:
o: Performs procedures designed to identify events that may require adjustment/disclosure
questions.why: SA 560: during the period (date of statements → date of auditor's report) the auditor performs specific procedures (review minutes, latest interim, inquiry) — 'no active search' applies only AFTER report date; before it, the obligation runs.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — 'no responsibility' starts at the report date, not at year-end AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: No active search after report date

questions.q: If management refuses to provide a required written representation, the auditor should FIRST:
o: Discuss with management, reassess management's integrity, and evaluate the effect on the opinion — including possible withdrawal
Ignore it as it is 'just' a form
questions.why: Refusal → discuss, evaluate the representation's importance for obtaining sufficient appropriate evidence, reconsider integrity (fraud implications), take appropriate action; a scope-limitation path to qualified/disclaimer — withdrawal may be needed — not an instant-adverse reflex.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — a missing signature is first an integrity alarm, then an opinion event AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The form is paper; the refusal is a statement.

questions.q: Where a material uncertainty exists and is adequately disclosed in the financial statements, the auditor (under current SAs) issues:
o: An unmodified opinion with a 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' section
questions.why: SA 570: adequate disclosure ⇒ unmodified + the dedicated MUTRC section (the 2021-style architecture moved uncertainty emphasis from an EOM paragraph to the report body); inadequate disclosure ⇒ modify (qualified/adverse by pervasiveness).
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — disclosed uncertainty ≠ modified opinion — but it must be said LOUD Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: The storm is disclosed; the captain signs off anyway.

questions.q: Management's going-concern assessment must cover at least:
o: 12 months from the date of financial statements (not the report)
questions.why: SA 570 requires management's evaluation to span at least 12 months from the date of the financial statements (auditors extend consideration if their own evaluation runs beyond, to the report date).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the clock starts at the statement date — know both dates AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Twelve months, counted from the numbers, not from the signature.

o: Individually AND in aggregate, against materiality and qualitatively
Only in the final audit file
questions.why: SA 450: the effect of each and the aggregate against overall materiality, plus QUALITATIVE factors (segment trends, debt covenants, ratios to avoid a negative turn, bias indicators) — 'immaterial' items in a biased direction can be material in context.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).

questions.q: Which is an ADJUSTING event after the year-end?
o: Insolvent customer whose collapse confirms December's doubtful state
questions.why: Confirmation of a year-end condition (the customer was already failing) ⇒ adjust the receivables/provision.
